title: Print a shared node once
starter:
type e = Lit of int | Var of string | Add of e * e | Mul of e * e

let emit (e : e) : string list * string =
  let lines = ref [] in
  let names : (e * string) list ref = ref [] in
  let rec go e =
    match e with
    | Lit n -> string_of_int n
    | Var s -> s
    | Add (a, b) | Mul (a, b) ->
      let x = go a in
      let y = go b in
      let op = match e with Add _ -> "+" | _ -> "*" in
      let v = Printf.sprintf "v%d" (List.length !lines) in
      lines := Printf.sprintf "int32_t %s = (int32_t)((uint32_t)%s %s (uint32_t)%s);" v x op y :: !lines;
      v
  in
  let result = go e in
  ignore names;
  (List.rev !lines, result)

samples.expr: (let x = Add (Var "a", Lit 1) in emit (Mul (x, x)))
samples.label: (let x = Add (Var "a", Lit 1) in emit (Mul (x, x)))

hints: The table `names` is there and nothing uses it yet. It should pair a node you have already printed with the C name you gave it.
`List.assq_opt e !names` looks a node up with `==`, which asks whether two values are the very same node. Two nodes that were built separately stay separate even when they look equal.
Wrap the branch: `match List.assq_opt e !names with Some v -> v | None -> ...` and, in the `None` case, add `names := (e, v) :: !names;` just before the final `v`.

answer.code:
type e = Lit of int | Var of string | Add of e * e | Mul of e * e

let emit (e : e) : string list * string =
  let lines = ref [] in
  let names : (e * string) list ref = ref [] in
  let rec go e =
    match e with
    | Lit n -> string_of_int n
    | Var s -> s
    | Add (a, b) | Mul (a, b) ->
      (match List.assq_opt e !names with
       | Some v -> v
       | None ->
        let x = go a in
        let y = go b in
        let op = match e with Add _ -> "+" | _ -> "*" in
        let v = Printf.sprintf "v%d" (List.length !lines) in
        lines := Printf.sprintf "int32_t %s = (int32_t)((uint32_t)%s %s (uint32_t)%s);" v x op y :: !lines;
        names := (e, v) :: !names;
        v)
  in
  let result = go e in
  ignore names;
  (List.rev !lines, result)
answer.explain: The reference looks the node up in `names` with `List.assq_opt` before it walks into the sources, and returns the saved name when it is there. After printing a line it saves the pair of node and name. A node used twice is now printed once, and because the lookup comes first, its sources are not walked a second time either.
